page.layout: One printed page, with the edge of the neighbouring page at the right, which is not transcribed. Top: title block, centred, with "Aut" and a brace beside two lines. Then a verse reference, a Greek and Latin quotation, and one column of running text, justified, with a catchword at the bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO TERTIA.
In quâ ostenditur, non esse ad conscientiæ securitatem satis præsidii in virorum
GAL. II. 13.
main_text.p: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ[?]—— Ac simulabant una cum eo reliqui etiam Ju-dai, adeo ut Barnabas simul abduce-retur eorum simulatione.

I. CUM mihi propositum esset propriam & adæquatam Conscientiæ Regulam, quæ nobis certa esset & tuta vivendi lex, investigare: pernecessarium duxi ante ostendere, quàm gravi & periculoso in errore versentur ii, qui in rebus agendis Conscientiæ suæ securitati satis prospectum putant, si aut boni finis intentione, aut Sancti alicujus exemplo, aut viri eruditione pietatéq; insignis judicio & authori-tate, se factaque sua quoquo modo tueri poterunt. Et

page.notes: The page number "54" is printed at top left, with a stray mark after it that may be a fault, so it is doubtful. The Greek line is read with uncertainty in the middle word (συνυπεκρίθησαν); it is marked [?] at the end of the line, not in the word. The Greek opening "καὶ" was printed in a form close to Latin letters; it is read as Greek. The faint line above the title rules is show-through from the other side and is not transcribed. The right-hand edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
